texts.preamble: G.Kamaraj vs State Rep.By on 29 January, 2024 Author: N.Anand Venkatesh Bench: N.Anand Venkatesh Crl.O.P.No. In The High Court Of Judicature At Madras Dated : 29.01.2024 Coram The Honourable Mr Justice N.Anand Venkatesh Crl.O.P.No.2722 of 2023 and Crl.M.P.Nos.1587 and 1589 of 2023 G.Kamaraj ... Petition Vs. State rep.by Food Safety Officer, Code No.061, Kodumudi Block, Tamil Nadu Food Safety and Drug Administration Department, Government Hospital Complex, Erode 638 102. ... Respondent Prayer : Criminal Original Petition has been filed under Section 48 Cr.P.C. to call for the records in C.C.No.28 of 2019 on the file of District Munsif cum Judicial Magistrate, Kodumudi and to quash the For Petitioner : Mr.P.Kannan Kumar For Respondent : Mr.A.Gopinath Government Advocate (Crl.Sid Page 1 of 6 https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Crl Order
texts.facts: There was delay in analysing the sample and submitting the report. Next submissions is that, though samples were taken on 29.03.2013, the complaint was filed before the learned Judicial Magistrate only on 24.11.2017, beyond the period of one year limitation. 4. The case of the respondent is that the Rice Mill belonging to the petitioner was inspected by the designated Officer on 29.03.2023. The premises was kept in lock and key. Thereafter, an FIR came to be registered and the premises was opened. It was found that the petitioner was in possession of adulterated food product. A sample was taken and it was forwarded to the Food Analysis Laboratory at Coimbatore. The report of the Food Analysis Laboratory was thereafter forwarded to the designated Officer on 10.04.2013 and he opined that the sample was found to be adulterated. Thereafter, the complaint came to be filed on 24.11.2017. 5.
texts.arguments: The main ground that was urged by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the complaint itself is barred since it has been filed beyond the period of one year limitation provided under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The delay seems to have occasioned due to delay in getting the Sanction Order from the competent authority. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6 Section 77 of the Act provides for time limit for prosecution. This provision makes it clear that a Court cannot take cognizance of the offence under the Act, if the period of one year from the date of commission of the offence expires, provided that the Commissioner of food safety, may for reasons to be recorded in writing, approve prosecution within an extended period of upto three years.
texts.petitioner_arguments: The main ground that was urged by the learned counsel for the petitioner is that the complaint itself is barred since it has been filed beyond the period of one year limitation provided under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The delay seems to have occasioned due to delay in getting the Sanction Order from the competent authority. https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 6
